Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Goal: Build a RAG-powered internal search + assistant for 50k documents (product specs, support articles, contracts). Primary success metrics: grounding_rate >= 90% and average helpfulness score >= 4.2 (scale 1-5) on sampled prompts.
- Constraints: low-latency targets (p95 generation < 750ms for chat flows), and cost target to be under $0.015 per convo on average during POC.
- Risks: legal content requires strict grounding and auditability; procurement will ask for SOC2 evidence and retention/audit logs.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) POC scope: 2-week evaluation using a ~10k doc subset (mix of long specs + short KB articles).
2) Redwood will provide: benchmark results (embedding + retrieval), a starter prompt set (attached), recommended model & reranker matrix, and a short eval harness you can run in-house.
3) ACME: confirm POC start date (we suggested Aug 23) and share any must-have queries or failure cases to include in eval.

Samir — thanks, good asks. Sharing a concise recommendation below and I’ve dropped the benchmark folder and prompt set to the Drive link. Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.txt + a metrics CSV snapshot.

Recommended model stacks (POC):
A) Accuracy-first (higher cost):
 - Retriever: rw-embed-14B (dense), vector index: HNSW, candidate pool: 50
 - Reranker: RW-cross-enc-1.2 (cross-encoder re-ranker) — re-rank top 10
 - Generator: RW-Chat-13B-q4 (chat model, q4 quantized)
 - Expected: p95 gen ~650–800ms (depending on infra), target per-convo cost ~$0.020–0.030 during POC

B) Cost-optimized (lower cost, slightly lower recall):
 - Retriever: rw-embed-2B (dense smaller), index: FAISS IVF+PQ, candidate pool: 100
 - Reranker: RW-light-rerank-1 (bi-encoder + fast cross scoring) — re-rank top 5
 - Generator: RW-Base-3B (optimized)
 - Expected: p95 gen ~350–550ms, target per-convo cost ~$0.007–0.012

Notes on grounding & eval: 
- We recommend measuring grounding_rate (percentage of answers with >=1 verifiable citation), hallucination_rate (manual spot checks), precision@k for retriever, and end-to-end helpfulness score.
- I’ve added a short README in the Drive explaining how to run the benchmark harness and reproduce the CSV. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ACME-EVAL-2027

Rishi / Neha / Vivek — please add any tweaks (indexing settings, chunk size, overlap) before I send this to ACME as the POC matrix.

Quick technical notes & recommended defaults for the POC — pulling from our internal RAG playbook: 

Retrieval / indexing:
- Chunking: 400–600 token chunks with 128 token overlap works well for long specs (captures context and keeps passages coherent).
- Embedding model: rw-embed-14B for accuracy; fall back to rw-embed-2B for cost runs.
- Index: HNSW for low-latency nearest-neighbor; if you need more throughput per node, FAISS IVF+PQ is a lower-cost option.
- Candidate pool (recall phase): 50–200 depending on the retriever; start with 100 for cost-optimized, 50 for accuracy-first.

Reranker:
- Recommendation: use a cross-encoder style reranker (RW-cross-enc-1.2) for the accuracy-first variant — re-rank top 10 and surface the top 3 citations inline.
- For cost-optimized, a bi-encoder + lightweight scoring (RW-light-rerank-1) is acceptable; re-rank top 5.
- Note: cross-encoders are more compute expensive but materially improve grounding precision on short KB passages.

Grounding metrics & checks:
- grounding_rate: percent of responses that include >=1 citation to an indexed doc
- citation_precision@k: manual/automatic checks to ensure cited spans actually support the claim
- hallucination_rate: proportion of answers flagged in manual spot-checks as unverifiable/incorrect
- latency and cost per convo tracked separately.

Quality regression & quantization caveats: 
- Moving to q4 quantization (RW-Chat-13B-q4) can reduce quality on nuanced legal phrasing. Strongly recommend per-prompt regression tests: take a 200-query golden set (including legal edge cases) and compare LLM outputs across model variants (BLEU/ROUGE not sufficient — use human helpfulness labels or automated grounding checks).
- Set automatic regression alerts if helpfulness score drops >5% or hallucination_rate increases >3% compared to baseline.

Evaluation harness & next steps:
1) ACME: drop the 200 golden queries / failure cases in the Drive folder.
2) Redwood: we’ll run the initial benchmark (both stacks) and push the CSV + a short report (expected in 48–72 hours after we get the golden set).
3) Decide on POC infra: hosted Redwood API vs dedicated instance (we can price both) — for initial runs hosted will be fastest.

I attached a short PDF with reranker tradeoffs and example metrics (redwood-reranker-recs.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick SE call tomorrow if you want to walk the settings.
